agree.reason: The two commissioners focused on traffic hear only that a D is 'not failing' and a vague request to review signal timing, so the speech gives them no concrete reason to vote yes, though the waiting-list case may move a few neighbours.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief and 'one in six' (64/412) holds up, but 'no one is pushed out' and the claim that every household gets a space assume more than the facts support.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns 64 of 412 into one in six and frames the 72 spaces as eight to spare, but it doesn't use the signal fact that keeps the intersection at C, which would have been the strongest true version of the traffic numbers.

right_comparison.reason: The 'if turned down, nothing changes' passage describes the status quo plainly (empty lot, 2,100 short, 412 waiting), though it doesn't say whether the shortage is growing.

qualification.reason: The only condition is a loose 'review the signal timing', when the obvious checkable condition was a builder-funded signal that keeps Alder and 4th at a C, and it gives no date or consequence if that isn't met.

objections.reason: Parking is answered, but the main traffic objection is met by minimizing it rather than with the signal offer, and the speech ignores 20 months of construction trucks, existing morning backups and the neighbour-parking commitment.

fit.reason: At roughly 350 words it fits a 3-minute spoken slot and reads well aloud, but it leaves [NAME] and [CHURCH NAME] as placeholders even though the user gave both.
